SquIP: The Master Equations

SquIP is an infinite system of differential equations describing the dynamics of the distribution of the MoI in a cohort of humans as it ages.

The system has three classes of variable:

  • SS describes the density of susceptible individuals

  • PP describes the density of chemo-protected individuals

  • IiI_i describes the density of individuals infected with exactly ii parasite types

The model has several parameters that could vary with respect to age:

  • μ\mu is the death rate of the cohort with respect to age

  • hh is the force of infection (FoI), the rate that infections occur

  • rr is the rate that each clone clears, and we assume that each parasite clone clears independently of the others at a constant rate, regardless of the age of the clone

  • ρ\rho is the fraction of incident infections that are treated and cured

  • ξ\xi is the rate that people take drugs and cure infections without regard to whether they are infected

  • σ\sigma is the rate that people take drugs and cure infections because they are infected, so that anyone who is infected would cure infections at the rate σ+ξ\sigma + \xi

  • η\eta is the rate that chemoprotection is lost after curing an infection

Dynamics

The dynamics of susceptible and chemoprotected individuals are:

dPda=−ηP+(hρ+ξ)(S+I)+σI−μPdSda=ηP+rI1−(h+μ+ξ)S\begin{equation} \begin{array}{rl} \frac{dP}{da} &= - \eta P + (h \rho + \xi) \left( S + I \right) + \sigma I -\mu P\\ \frac{dS}{da} &= \eta P + r I_1 - (h + \mu + \xi) S \end{array} \end{equation}

We track the number infected with ii types, Ii.I_i.

dI1da=2rI2+h(1−ρ)S−(r+h+σ+ξ+μ)I1dI2da=3rI3+h(1−ρ)I1−(2r+h+σ+ξ+μ)I2dIida=irIi+h(1−ρ)Ii−1−(ir+h+σ+ξ+μ)Ii\begin{equation} \begin{array}{rl} \frac{dI_1}{da} &= 2r I_2 + h (1-\rho) S - (r + h + \sigma + \xi + \mu ) I_1 \\ \frac{dI_2}{da} &= 3r I_3 + h (1-\rho) I_1 - (2r + h + \sigma + \xi + \mu) I_2 \\ \frac{dI_i}{da} &= ir I_i + h (1-\rho) I_{i-1} - (ir + h + \sigma + \xi + \mu) I_i \\ \end{array} \end{equation}

The implementation truncates the infinite system, choosing a largest MoI, nn:

dInda=h(1−ρ)In−1−(nr+hρ+σ+ξ+μ)In\begin{equation} \frac{dI_n}{da} = h (1-\rho) I_{n-1} - (n r + h \rho + \sigma + \xi+ \mu) I_n \end{equation}

In this implementation, the function solve_SquIP solves the equations and then it computes the first two moments of the distribution:

m=1H∑iiIim = \frac 1 H \sum_i i I_i

and

m2=1H∑ii2Iim_2 = \frac 1 H \sum_i i^2 I_i

In SIPm (below), we derive equations to compute dm/dadm/da and dm2/da.d m_2 /da.

denote the mean MoI in the population. We can show that

dmda=h(1−ρ)(1−PH)−(r+ρh+σ+ξ)m \frac{\textstyle{dm}}{\textstyle{da}} = h(1-\rho)\left(1-\frac{P}{H} \right) - \left(r + \rho h + \sigma + \xi \right) m We also compute the 2nd moment:

dm2da=h(1−ρ)(1−PH+2m)−(2r+ρh+σ+ξ)m2+rm \frac{\textstyle{dm_2}}{\textstyle{da}} = h(1-\rho)\left(1-\frac{P}{H} + 2m\right) - \left(2r + \rho h + \sigma + \xi \right) m_2 + r m

The function solveSIPqueue:

  • calls d_SIPqueue_da which computes all the derivaves for SS, II, PP, and mm

  • computes mm from II

foiP1 = list(hbar = 1, agePar = par_flatAge(), seasonPar = par_flatSeason(), trendPar = par_flatTrend())
q_out <- solve_SquIP(8/365, sigma=2/365, xi=0, foiP1, Amax=5*365)

For verification, the variable mm is computed two ways We note that the variable mm matches the MoI computed from II:

with(q_out, plot(age, m, type = "l"))
with(q_out, lines(age, mm, lty=2, col = "yellow"))
with(q_out, plot(age, m2, type = "l", ylim = range(m2, mm2)))
with(q_out, lines(age, mm2, lty=2, col = "yellow"))

Approximating Equations

dPda=−ηP+(hρ+ξ)(S+I)+σI−μPdSda=ηP+Fr(m,m2)I−(h+μ+ξ)SdIda=h(1−ρ)S−Fr((m,m2))I−(hρ+σ+ξ)S−μS\begin{equation} \begin{array}{rl} \frac{dP}{da} &= - \eta P + (h \rho + \xi) \left( S + I \right) + \sigma I -\mu P\\ \frac{dS}{da} &= \eta P + F_r(m, m_2) I - (h + \mu + \xi) S \\ \frac{dI}{da} &= h(1-\rho) S - F_r((m, m_2)) I - (h \rho + \sigma + \xi) S - \mu S \end{array} \end{equation}

We compute mm and m2m_2 as before, and we let

Fr=rdnbinom(1,m,size=ϕ)1−dnbinom(0,m,size=ϕ))(1−PH)F_r = r \frac{\mbox{dnbinom}(1, m, \mbox{size} = \phi)}{1-\mbox{dnbinom}(0, m, \mbox{size} =\phi))}\left(1-\frac P H \right)

where ϕ=m2m2−m2−m\phi = \frac{m^2}{m_2-m^2-m}

m_out <- solveSIPm(8/365, sigma=2/365, xi=0, foiP1, Amax=5*365)
with(m_out, plot(age, S, ylim = c(0,1000), type = "l"))
with(m_out, lines(age, I))
with(m_out, lines(age, P))
with(q_out, lines(age, S, col = "yellow", lty=2))
with(q_out, lines(age, I, col = "yellow", lty=2))
with(q_out, lines(age, P, col = "yellow", lty=2))
with(q_out, plot(age, Fr, type = "l", ylim = c(0, 0.005)))
with(m_out, lines(age, c(.005, Fr), col = "red"))
with(m_out, plot(age, m, type = "l"))
with(q_out, lines(age, m, lty=2, col = "yellow"))
with(m_out, plot(age, m2, type = "l"))
with(q_out, lines(age, m2, lty=2, col = "yellow"))
